title: Machine learning based prediction of microbiological findings and infectious focus determination in adult intensive care patients
summary:
Severe infections represent a major challenge in intensive care units, as the causative pathogen and the exact source of infection often can only be clearly identified after several days of microbiological testing. During this time, physicians frequently have to treat patients with broad-spectrum antibiotics, which may promote the development of antibiotic resistance.

In this study, routinely collected clinical data from adult patients treated in intensive care units at Heidelberg University Hospital between 2019 and 2024 are retrospectively analyzed. The aim is to train a predictive model using modern artificial intelligence methods that can predict, based on clinical parameters and laboratory values, whether a blood culture will be positive or negative and which type of pathogen is most likely present. In the long term, such a predictive model may help to enable faster and more targeted treatment of infections.

interventions.name: In this retrospective, monocentric study, routine clinical data of adult patients treated between 2019 and 2024 in anesthesiology-led intensive care units at Heidelberg University Hospital are analyzed. All included patients had at least one blood culture taken during their ICU stay. No intervention

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Collection of at least one blood culture during the intensive care unit stay
Exclusion criteria:
Missing or incomplete data on blood culture results
